svg.text: Detection & Analysis — a P0 found by elimination, not by luck
Every step ruled something out — narrating that method is what the interviewer is actually grading
T+0 · L2 raises P1 — “login failing in driver app” (24 h SLA)
Impact looks narrow → we scope to the driver app first. Assumption — and it costs us time.
Interview line: “we concentrated on the reported area; escalation taught us to verify reach early.”
T+5 min · Reporter tries a WhatsApp OTP — it works
Ruled out: authentication + OTP generation are fine. Suspect now: delivery channels only.
This tiny experiment split “login is broken” from “OTP is not arriving” in minutes.
T+30 min · Escalations from buyer app + vendor portal → promoted to P0
All three apps affected → immediate attention. Severity grows, scope widens — now it is a P0.
Incident priorities: P1 = resolve inside SLA (~24 h) · P0 = service down, immediate action.
T+35 min · As the owner: check deployments and recent changes
Nothing deployed, nothing changed in the code → ruled out: a regression from our own release.
“No code change + service degraded” pointed outside our app — to delivery and the provider.
T+40 min · Server logs — not sufficient
Provider responses were never logged, so “sent” looked normal. Detection gap identified.
Lesson said out loud: monitor at the dependency boundary, not only inside your own logs.
T+50 min · Data platform: query login-success rate over the last hours
Success rate has collapsed → ruled out: narrow blast radius or user error. It is delivery-wide.
Data before guesses — a strong, interview-visible habit for root-cause analysis.
T+60 min · Provider portal → root cause found
DLT registration was BLOCKED — every SMS OTP is rejected at the operator, silently.
A fresh DLT registration takes ~4 days → waiting is impossible, the fix must reroute.
